items.prompt:
A population is:
A) All living things in the world
B) All members of one species in the same area
C) One organism
D) Only plants
items.answer: B) All members of one species in the same area

steps: A population is one species living in one area.

items.prompt:
Which is a resource that affects population size?
A) Food
B) A memory
C) A chromosome
D) An organelle

steps: Food is a resource populations depend on.

items.prompt:
When resources are plentiful, a population tends to:
A) Grow
B) Disappear
C) Stay frozen forever
D) Become one species

steps: Plenty of resources supports population growth.

items.prompt:
A resource or condition that restricts population growth is a:
A) Producer
B) Limiting factor
C) Consumer
D) Decomposer

steps: Limiting factors cap how large a population can grow.

items.prompt:
A drought kills many plants that deer eat. The deer population will most likely:
A) Increase
B) Decrease
C) Stay exactly the same
D) Turn into plants

steps: Less food limits how many deer can survive, so the population falls.

items.prompt:
Two ponds are the same size, but one has more food. That pond will likely support:
A) Fewer fish
B) A larger fish population
C) No fish
D) Only plants

A graph shows a rabbit population rise, then crash right after a hard winter reduced grass. The best conclusion is:
A) Winter increased food
B) Reduced food (a limiting factor) caused the crash
C) Rabbits need no food
D) Grass is a consumer
items.answer: B) Reduced food (a limiting factor) caused the crash

steps: The food shortage acted as a limiting factor, causing the population to crash.

items.prompt:
To test whether water is a limiting factor for a plant population, you should compare areas that differ in:
A) The amount of water, keeping other conditions similar
B) Everything at once
C) Only the plant species
D) Nothing
items.answer: A) The amount of water, keeping other conditions similar

steps: Changing only water isolates its effect as a limiting factor.
